criteria.notes: Closed by a green run this pass produced. THE PID-WALK KILL MECHANISM HAD NEVER EXECUTED LIVE BEFORE THIS RUN (wi5 §8 records it as unexercised). Had the walk misbehaved that would have been a TEST defect to file rather than a subject failure, and the two would have been distinguished per the brief's "the subject held; the test did not" ruling. It did not arise. WHY THE ASSERTIONS ARE NON-VACUOUS, checked rather than assumed: the fork-isolation claim is byte identity of the original transcript (:322), not a summary property, and it is paired with :319's proof that the fork's OWN transcript is non-empty — so "the fork did nothing" cannot satisfy it. Every no-interleave absence is paired with a positive control on the same transcript (:425-428). And :348-362 records a real earlier vacuity in this very arm — the engine REFUSED the original token-echo framing, failing the test on its design rather than on the product — which is exactly why the current framing reads a file that genuinely exists on disk.

The cost is not avoided by the red arriving early — `npm run test:live` carries no `--bail`, so all 17 files run regardless of order (measured: 17 of 17 ran in a zero-spend, gate-refused run this pass captured), meaning the full engine-claude suite — roughly 60-90 haiku invocations — is spent to reach a millisecond failure, and spent AGAIN on the eventual real dispatch.
